rv.q: I’m pleased to report that this genial condensing of three episodes delivers a hugely entertaining blast of unadorned nostalgia.
This leaves us wanting more, much more.
It is too funny to quibble too long about its provenance.
I suggest you book an en suite.
He embodies the character both vocally, with an uncanny likeness to Cleese, and physically - all bendy rubberiness - and captures the splenetic outbursts, the waspish asides and inner pain.
As those cheers rightly suggest, this Fawlty Towers redux is no pale imitation of the original, but a very vivid one.

Even so, and despite the live-event bonus of different generations coming together, as they once gathered round the box, to watch it as one, I can’t avoid noting that the show falls far short of its peerless source material.
There are many hugely entertaining, well-known exchanges, but it doesn’t really add up to a fully formed play.
But, overall, it’s a chance to check in for some familiar dishes rather than sample anything fresh.

The lines, the laughs, even the accents and intonations of the greatest British sitcom ever, Fawlty Towers, are present and correct in this efficient and energetic stage adaptation, but it’s an oddly soulless affair.
We’re left anticipating old laughs rather than being surprised by new ones.
The show does exactly what it says on the tin – it takes Fawlty-world on to the boards and gives it live, three-dimensional flesh.
This is theatrical time travel of the most joyful variety.
The result is a very funny and entertaining evening, one that is remarkably faithful to the original material.
The end product does not disappoint.
For anyone who saw the sitcom in the 1970s, this is a pleasantly weird show.

The result, which is certainly not “a play”, has all the carefully crafted comedy of the original, with the only real difference being that there are no close-ups and one or two lines have to be delivered at full volume.
But for all its wistful charm it’s hard to escape the feeling that this is also a cynical product.
Fantastic in every respect, I really can’t fault it.
It’s the funniest show in town.
If it were just a nostalgia exercise it would have limited appeal but what is essentially a farce shot on a fixed TV set works very well on stage.
If you're a die-hard fan of the original series and are keen to see it be brought to life on-stage, you won't be disappointed.
The result is spectacularly funny.
In fact it is everything one could hope for.
It might not be challenging theatre, but it's a nostalgic joy, much like watching an episode of the original show.

cn.t: Critics find this faithful stage adaptation of the classic sitcom technically skillful and crowd-pleasing, but most question its artistic necessity, calling it polished nostalgia that lacks soul despite strong performances.
